name: sudo-command-center (teaching edition)
_comment_include: Everything the system needs to run for someone who has no projects yet. Tool surface dirs (.claude/.opencode/.antigravity/.agent) are included so commands resolve on first clone rather than after a /sync-agents.
_comment_exclude: Personal, machine-local, or project-owned. _my_resources is Daniel's personal area; _artifacts is session memory; .gitnexus is a per-machine index; Projects/ holds real client work.
_comment_excludeAnywhere: Path segments never copied, wherever they appear.
_comment_substitutions: Most domain references in core commands are incidental examples, not structure. Matching is CASE-SENSITIVE so replacements read naturally in context (DANIEL in a heading becomes THE OPERATOR, not 'the operator'). That means every case variant needs its own row - the case-INSENSITIVE leak scan below is what proves none were missed. Order matters: longest first, so AGY_AVIATIONCHAT is consumed before AVIATIONCHAT.
_comment_transforms: Whole-file swaps for files whose CONTENT is personal, not just its tokens. operator-profile is floor-tier and hard-codes Daniel as chair; unchanged, a stranger's agent believes it is talking to him.
_comment_leakScan: Runs after every export and cannot be skipped. Any hit blocks the push. Matching is case-INSENSITIVE, so it catches case variants the substitution table missed - that is its main job. Every value from the live .env is added automatically. NOTE: _my_resources is deliberately NOT a needle. It is a structural folder name in the workspace standard (a personal area agents never touch) and the teaching edition should keep the concept; only its CONTENTS are excluded.
